doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

title: The third movement theme and the violin cadenza
summary: Rowe transcribed the third movement's opening; Sandoval discusses the demanding violin cadenza and consulting violinists about playability.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I would totally agree and it was so melodic, the third movement of this second concerto, that I pulled out some staff paper and I decided to do what I fifty some years ago had to

do in music school and that was write down your opening of the third movement. So if you’ll bear with me, you can be my professor to see how I did. Because let me see — [scats] and then back to the [scats]. And I was like oh, that’s so lovely.

Thank you sir, thank you, thank you. You know it’s something easy to remember, as you can see, and it has a simple line, just changing the chord underneath and I’m doing some counter line and things to develop the first idea.
Well it surely works and somewhere in there you wrote a finger-buster of a first violin solo. Do you remember that part?

Yeah. It’s like a cadenza. For the concert master. Yeah. You know I hear Ruben playing it in Europe and some of the violin players did it okay. Some, very few, did it well. And the others they’re the worst. Because they cannot take it for granted, you know, they have to spend a few minutes practicing that cadenza. Yeah. If they practice it and get it down it’s okay. But you know in a way, when I wrote it I talked to a couple of good, good violin players here in town and I consulted them about it, that it was playable. Is this something the violin could do. They said absolutely, it’s just a matter of spending some time and really getting it down.

Yeah that’s one of the big challenges of writing for orchestras is knowing what instruments can actually pull off and you have to do a little bit of research and of course talking to people like that is very helpful. I want to see if we can get rid of the — there’s feedback happening on my end so could you go back to that audio setting page.
